notes:
Oregon's recurring entity-level levy on an LLC is the Corporate Activity Tax (CAT), ORS 317A. It passes the inclusion test on the statute's own terms: ORS 317A.116(1) imposes it on each person with taxable commercial activity for the privilege of doing business in this state, ORS 317A.100(14) defines a person to include limited liability companies, and it is annual (ORS 317A.137's annual return) and measured on commercial activity. The label is the state's own: 'Corporate Activity Tax'. basis is revenue: the amount scales with commercial activity (total amount realized from transactions and activity, without deduction for expenses). minimumAnnualUsd is 0, the published no-tax-due case: ORS 317A.125(2) says a tax is not owed if taxable commercial activity does not exceed $1 million, and the Department's own page says only taxpayers with more than $1 million of taxable Oregon commercial activity have a payment obligation. Above that the floor is the $250 flat component plus 0.57 percent of the excess. Registration begins at $750,000 (ORS 317A.131), filing above $1 million (ORS 317A.137), and the return is due the 15th day of the fourth month following the end of the tax year. This is the Ohio-CAT shape, threshold-gated with a $0 minimum for an ordinary LLC, and there is no first-year waiver: the obligation attaches to the year's activity from the first year the thresholds are crossed.
The corporation excise tax and its minimum tax are excluded: the Department's own Corporation Excise and Income Tax page imposes them on corporations, and its FAQ answers 'I'm a limited liability company (LLC). How do I file in Oregon?' with 'File the same way for Oregon as you did for federal' - a partnership-taxed LLC files a partnership return, so the corporate minimum tax does not reach a default LLC.
collectedWithAnnualReport is false: root states.json carries annual_report_fee 100 for Oregon, the Secretary of State's annual report fee, a separate payment with no tax to overlap. The CAT is filed with the Oregon Department of Revenue.
stateIncomeTax: members owe Oregon personal income tax on pass-through income. The 2025 Form OR-40 instructions put the top marginal rate at 9.9% (Chart S, over $125,000). Oregon created the Pass-Through Entity Elective (PTE-E) Tax for tax years beginning on or after 2022-01-01: entities taxed as S corporations and partnerships may elect annually to pay 9 percent on the first $250,000 of distributive proceeds and 9.9 percent on the excess, with members claiming a credit on their individual returns; the law expires if the federal SALT deduction limitation expires or is repealed.
needsReview: The CAT statute (ORS 317A) was read from the legislature's chapter page and the collector's pages were read in full, so nothing recorded here is ungrounded. What is missing is only the 2026 regular session's amendment-and-repeal table referenced at the top of the ORS chapter page: the text read is the 2025 Edition, and the chapter page notes that sections were amended or repealed during the 2026 regular session. Reading the 2026 A&R table would confirm no recorded figure changed before the 2026 tax year.
